The Bookbinder's Bargain #1

Kiss of the Black Flame

Helen Scheuerer

4.09
6,996 ratings2,422 reviews
Rate this book
Some bargains are sealed with blood...Others with fire...The deadliest are sealed with a kiss...

Saige Grayson has always believed stories could heal—even when her own body refuses to. As the most promising bookbinder in the capital, she’s learned to work through chronic pain and crushing debt, restoring other people’s treasures while trying not to fall apart herself. But when the man she owes decides her rare talent is worth more than her payments, Saige is traded to the Azkari—an immortal race forged by the gods for war—and imprisoned in their ancient stronghold.

Her only chance of survival lies with Archer, a fallen Azkari general imprisoned beside her —cursed, dangerous, and impossible to ignore. He offers her a way out, and in return, Saige must help him retrieve and restore an ancient book. But the book is made of living magic, powerful enough to stop a great evil—or unleash it. And as Saige works with Archer, the tome begins to awaken something dark and dangerous—both in the realm and within her.

As their enemies close in and buried memories resurface, Saige and Archer must decide what they’re willing to their freedom, their fragile trust…or the spark that could ignite the world.

About the author

Helen Scheuerer

49 books8,140 followers
Helen Scheuerer is the fantasy author of the bestselling series, The Oremere Chronicles, the Curse of the Cyren Queen quartet and The Legends of Thezmarr. Her work has been highly praised for its strong, flawed female characters and its action-packed plots.

Helen’s love of writing and books led her to pursue a creative writing degree and a Masters of Publishing. She has been a full-time author since 2018 and now lives amidst the mountains in New Zealand where she is constantly dreaming up new stories.

Liana Gold
639 reviews615 followers
Review of advance copy received from NetGalley
June 17, 2026
LUSTY BOOKS are not my thing. After 3 disappointing fantasies, this marks my 4th. I was very excited to dive into my first Helen Scheuerer book and I know she is a very well loved author, but this story didn't work for me at all.

1. Despite being marketed as a slow burn, this is very much an insta-love story where the MMC by 19% is stating that this woman is the bane of his existence and the FMC has already sexual thoughts of him. By 25%, the MMC says she makes him feel alive.. Calm your horses down, you just met.
The emotional stakes were LOW, the romance overall is surface level. There was absolutely no chemistry, it’s all spice spice spice. If that’s your thing, this book will be for you! I don’t want to waste my time reading books that absolutely do not deliver.

2. This is a fantasy.. so where is the world building? What is the threat? Where is the sense of urgency? There is a 'villain' in the story ... but WHY is he absent in the book? What is he actually doing? what is a larger political situation??

3. Unnecessarily clunky and middle drags.. what is actually happening? Lots of repetition.



I will justify my low star review in my expanded review when I have a chance to sit down and write it out.





Many thanks to NetGalley, Atria Books and the author, Helen Scheuerer for an early copy!

2.5⭐️ I am disappointed. I wanted to love this SO badly, but it fell very short of my expectations. I almost DNF’d but ultimately decided to push through.

Let’s start with what I did enjoy. I loved the FMC, Saige. As someone living with chronic illness, I found the chronic pain representation very accurate. I appreciated that the author made Saige’s pain a recurring part of her journey rather than a label haphazardly added for inclusivity points. Her struggles were relatable, and I admired her relentless optimism and maturity despite everything life threw at her.

On the other hand, I struggled to like the MMC, Archer. I’m usually a fan of broody MMCs… as long as there’s a good reason for it! Archer’s initial harshness and coldness toward Saige felt unjustified and didn’t make much sense within the context of their relationship, which made it difficult for me to empathize with him.

And I know I’ve mentioned this before, but I despise fast-burn and insta-lust romances. I was caught off guard when Saige and Archer were lusting after one another after knowing each other for barely 10 minutes. It’s not necessarily a flaw of the book, but more so a matter of a personal preference. Archer also constantly flipped between flirting with Saige and suddenly pushing her away, insisting he wasn’t “good” for her, which gave me major emotional whiplash.

The world-building was extremely lacking, and the main antagonist was absent the entire book. I probably could have guessed the plot twist at the end if I wasn’t so frustrated with everything else. I can understand how other readers might enjoy this, but unfortunately, it just wasn’t for me😔

I screamed when this popped in my emails, a few months ago! NetGalley & Atria books ; you’ve made this girl so happy 🥹💗 (the boyfriend is used to the screaming now. He knows it’s always about books)
BR this with my twin Krysta 🥹❤️‍🔥 I’m soooo EXCITED!! (We had the same thoughts 🥺)

Having absolutely loved her most recent trilogy, I think it’s safe to say that I had really high expectations for this. Unfortunately, this novel did not work for me for various reasons.

The synopsis was very interesting ; a promising bookbinder that has to work with an imprisoned mmc to find & fix an evil book.

The thing is that there were more information about this book in the synopsis than in the actual story. The worldbuilding was a mix of lacking & absent. So much time was spent on how the characters were feeling rather than explaining the actual plot or why these things they were doing were so important. The story wants you to feel the sense of danger & urgency but it wasn’t in the room with us. The villain is supposed to be this very evil presence but what was he doing the whole book?

The characters were absolutely insufferable for me. I wanted to dnf because I could not stand them. The mmc was rude & lost to self pity. The fmc was so annoying & kind of pathetic towards the mmc? I don’t get why she wanted him so bad because he was just really rude to her (I mean, she was irritating tbh but that’s not the point).
It was insta lust to the max. The timeline was also really off because they were obsessed with each other within less than a few hours.
The fmc kept saying he was her mirror but I’ve never seen characters who were less alike.
She also kept throwing random temper tantrums and at 35, I think it was misplaced. And she always picked the worst moments too? The whole horse thing made me want to rip my eyebrows out. Get a grip. I just felt like I was reading iron flame all over again.

They had no chemistry and her thirst for him gave me major secondhand embarrassment.

A lot of things kept contradicting itself as the story went along. For example : he was made this way by the villain but then in flashbacks they keep calling him the black flame. So what did the villain make, aside from the brand? No training whatsoever but she threw a knife at him first glance and succeeded in killing a powerful soldier on her first try. The mmc’s brother saying they didn’t have time to prepare for war but it’s been 200 YEARS !!! What were you doing all that time?? Gallivanting around?? The fmc thirsting to know how the mmc was before his imprisonment and I just kept wondering what was the point? Trauma & healing changes you so why was this so important in that moment? To get the book they had to do this sort of truth or dare (that’s what it felt like for me) and it was so juvenile and awkward because then again, they didn’t have chemistry. And the mmc said she was the only one he trusted with his life but how embarrassing is that when he’s known her two days.

The most disappointing thing for me was how chronic pain was handled. I suffered from chronic pains from the ages of 17 to 21 and it was some of the toughest years of my life. I also care for people who live with it. And how she wrote chronic pain was really beside what it really is. Her flares only happened when it was convenient! Imagine if it was actually like that. I think it would’ve been better to not write this into the story because it’s just insulting at that point.

There’s a lot of instances where I just thought… this isn’t giving the punch you think it’s giving. They kept apologizing for what the other went through but it was over the top.

I thought maybe the ending would have made it worth it but I was also left dissatisfied & frankly irritated with how it was handled.

This was one of my most anticipated reads of the year so I’m feeling very letdown. I think this is going to work for a lot of people and I’m happy for them but it wasn’t for me.

3 stars for now ⭐️

I don't think I've ever felt so up and down about a book quite like this.. it was overall not what I was expecting to say the least, with good parts and bad parts. Many romantasy readers would definitely eat this up, but it just wasn't for me personally 🥹

The main reason I struggled with this was that it just felt so messy, right from the beginning. I went from enjoying at 10%, wanting to dnf at 30%, enjoying again until around 75% and then I just wanted to be done with it. It kind of reminded me of Metal Slinger in the way it panned out, so yeah. I also found it to be quite juvenile for a majority of it, and while I will say that this was an extremely ambitious fantasy with it's world building, magic system, politics and character backgrounds, you only really got that for 20% of the whole book and the other 80% was just heavy lustful romance.

Honestly, I really just want to move on from this book so I'll just bullet point instead 😅

things that worked for me:

- the actual concept of the fantasy world and history of the war was really interesting and intricate
- there were some lovely heartfelt quotes throughout and some important messaging woven in especially when it came to self doubt, mental illness, pain both physically and mentally etc
- Archer's character had good depth as the plot progressed
- there is a lot of potential for this world
- the scene setting was really good and I think the author did an amazing job in describing elements of the characters and places in the present tense
- the recovery of the book where they go through a trial was really unique and probably my favourite part, especially as it felt like a refreshing way for the main characters to speak their truths and the depth behind them to be built upon

things that didn't work for me:

- the world building/history/side characters weren't fleshed out enough and for a fantasy novel it was really lacking anything that wasn't romance
- it was insta-lust
- I understand wanting to add depth to the mmc, and it worked as the plot developed but for the first 30% I think that the grumpy x sunshine aspect was way overdone.. like I understand wanting him to be troubled after everything he's endured and struggling with human connection but it was to an extreme that was uncomfortable if that makes sense? it wasn't grumpiness, he was just an absolute dick and I think the way he spoke to the fmc was pushed too far for that early on in the book, especially considering what his character evolves into
- a lot of the writing felt forced? there is a lot of emphasis on this book being an advocation for chronic pain suffers etc, which I was excited for but between some of the quotes attributed to the fmc & the way feminist quotes were woven in (for example; continuous quips about women being paid less than men) sometimes it felt like a social media infographic instead of something from the reader herself. It also felt clear that there was a specific tagline being pushed, especially when it started to crop up almost every page near the end ()
- the plot twists were really obvious, which again made it feel a little juvenile
- character names/places/magical elements were introduced into dialogue with almost no explanation, so there was a lot of who/what/why/when/where
- not a lot actually happened aside from the fmc and mmc falling in love with each other, having miscommunication, making up and repeat cycle
- it did kind of feel like the author had a trope/plot device list and was trying to tick off as many as possible to sell to a certain audience (and basing it around what viral trends/attractive qualities there are)
- the twist at the end was not my favourite.. again, reminded me of metal slinger & obvs it's known I'm not a fan of that book

In conclusion, I don't think this is a bad book by any means. It's an okay book. I think it's probably going to be perfect for people who are coming from romance as a genre and maybe want to dip their toes into fantasy, and haven't read many other books from the genre yet. I think this is supposed to be a trilogy? Not sure I will continue the series personally, but I will be intrigued to see what the second book will look like in terms of plot development

i have so many issues with this book, so i think going the list route will save me at least some bit of rambling.

things i disliked :

• lack of world building
• insufferable, whining characters
• no chemistry whatsoever
• unclear knowledge of anything / confusion
• random character decisions
• the most irritating ending known to man
• completely unconvincing villain
• timeline’s don’t match up like they should

this was one of my most anticipated reads, i have read several books from this author though, so i was aware that sometimes her books will miss its mark for me.

Archer the mmc was always pitying himself & Saige the fmc was pushy and just annoying. i found their dynamic to be so odd for many reasons, Archer was so mean & rude to her & yet she’s obsessed with him? give me a damn break, let’s not be so desperate please. i think this first book shouldn’t have had any romance at all.

i had so many questions about things that should’ve been explained immediately. if this was going to be the case, i would’ve appreciated a glossary. nothing even happens in the slightest, it’s a lot of wasted time.

Malveron, the villain, is supposedly this huge threat but he’s absent the entire book. we’re told how they have to prepare against him, but 200+ years has gone by and everyone’s just been wandering around? there was no sense of urgency, so i couldn’t take anything seriously. i don’t even know if ill continue the series at this point, i really just didn’t have a good time reading this for real.

This book was gravity holding me down. Definitely one of the best books I’ve read in a while! Immediately after learning the FMC was a bookbinder, I wanted to read this, and starting with the “Dear readers,” letter I knew I’d like this author. I also adore and appreciate Saige represents so many characteristics and qualities that are not the norm in fantasy books.

Our FMC, Saige, is in her mid 30s, and she has chronic pain that the doctors can’t understand or find a cure for. This weaves its way into the feminism/ feminine rage portion of the story — because the men all believe she is faking the pain since they can’t see a cause or understand what’s happening. Saige is a very independent person (who is also stubborn and charming) and I love her for it. She really resonated with me.

The FMC & MMC have a lot of “I hate you but I’m attracted to you” banter, which I am a big fan of. I thought the story was entertaining throughout the book, and the writing style really helped me picture exactly what was happening in each scene. We go on an adventure to retrieve the book, and that’s when one of my favorite microtropes occurs: “you’re freezing, let me warm you up with body heat”

The setting is superb and works perfectly in the story: imagine cobblestone streets, the most quaint and picturesque bookbinding shop, and then we travel across the map in typical fantasy book style… and get even more locations that make me nostalgic for places I’ve never even been.

There are some twists and sneaky things that happen in the last portion of the book (at one point my jaw actually dropped). I was also surprised by the character reveals and learning the secrets that were kept. I can’t wait for the next book!

This was the first book I’ve read from this author, and now I really want to look into others! I hadn’t heard of her before this book, but since discovering it - I have seen a lot of positive things about her previous series.

-- Some bargains are sealed with blood. Others with fire. The deadliest are sealed with a kiss... --

The way that I fell in love with Saige and Archer could be slightly unhealty, as I love everything about them. 🥰 When Saige finds herself traded to the Azkari and locked in a prison, her only chance of escape is making a bargain with Archer, a fallen general that is imprisoned beside her. After sealing the bargain with a kiss, they embark on a journey to find and restore a book that might save their realm.

The relationship development between them is very well written. Over time, they slowly learn about each other, begin to trust, and realize they have more in common than they first realized. I loved their journey from barely tolerating each other into an intense connection that is hard for them to ignore.

Archer, reading shirtless with his slutty reading glasses nearly did me in! This man.. he's a bit broken, dark, and broody but he harbors a good heart under all that hard armor that he has built to protect himself. He is absolutely one of my new favorite book boyfriends.

Saige, who Archer calls by her last name Grayson, is a talented bookbinder who experiences unexplained chronic pain. She is the sunshine to Archer's darkness and I love her fiesty attitude.

-- “You can’t fix me, Grayson.”
But Saige lifts her chin defiantly.
“And you can’t break me, Archer.”--

When they finally stop fighting their feelings and that slow burn starts sparking, its hot and spicy and just 🥵🔥🫠😍

-- “So you may want to say a prayer to the Eternal Triad . . . Because gods, I’m about to ruin you, Saige.” --


I did figure out some of the plot twist pretty early on, but there was no way to know the full reveal and expect how it all played out. This book had me engaged and immersed all the way through and I am definitely all in on this series! I really enjoyed reading Kiss of the Black Flame and I cant wait for the next book to see what happens next.

☆ 4.5 stars

Kiss of the Black Flame is the first instalment in The Bookbinder’s Bargain trilogy by author Helen Scheuerer. This was an exciting and exhilarating new experience that found me on the edge of my seat for chapters on end in my anticipation to see what happens next. I wanted to cry every time I had to force myself to put my kindle down in-lieu of my adult responsibilities (wholly unfair if you ask me) and found myself counting down the minutes until I could pick it back up. Scheuerer is a phenomenal storyteller that knows how to write an addictive and compelling story that is filled with heartfelt found family connections, emotional dialogue and electrifying chemistry that will consume you from the very first page. The world established throughout this book feels darker and grittier than anything we have seen from this author before, and I loved getting to experience something brand new and exciting that I have never seen from her before. The world-building read with ease for me and I felt really intrigued by the magic system that is established from the very beginning which is something I hope to see continue to grow. Kiss of the Black Flame was the perfect cure to my ‘Thezmarr hangover’ and I cannot wait to continue to fall in-love with this universe in its entirety as much as I have that one.

Saige Grayson is yet another wonderfully strong heroine by this author that captured my heart from the very first page. Her experience in living with chronic pain and the way this impacts her everyday living felt seamlessly woven into her story in a manner that felt natural. I really appreciated that her pain wasn’t understated in its severity and the reality that enduring an invisible illness also results in facing disbelief and dismissal from her peers. Sage’s ability to view the world with openness and vulnerability in spite of all the harm that has been forced upon her is almost uncanny in its resolve. Her main strength exists within her mind alongside her capacity for kindness in a refusal to be confused for as meek. Her passion for her craft is undeniable and I adored witnessing the scenes where Saige’s own brand of (human) magic sparks to life when faced with a restoration project. Her character is effortlessly depicted in a way that feels relatable to the reader as I felt like her struggles became my struggles. Her burdens became my own to shoulder. I felt constantly in awe at everything Saige continued to carry physically, mentally and emotionally in her refusal to give up. There is no hurdle that she did not show a determination to navigate and I cannot express just how deeply I adore every aspect to the unwavering woman that she is written to be. Her selflessness and care for others is greatly reflected in the deep bonds she shares with Raven, Yevna and Grim. There is so much more to Saige’s character left to be uncovered and explored… and I cannot wait to see what comes next in her story throughout the continuation of this series.

If I were the kind of woman who barked at men then I would shamelessly be doing so when it comes to our mysterious general, Archer. His penchant for wearing slutty reading glasses whilst being depicted in his rugged state? Bark bark. Archer was everything that I had hoped he would be with his many intricate layers waiting to be unfurled and discovered. His grumpy and tortured demeanour felt perfectly balanced alongside his protective instincts and soft spot for the vulnerable. His trauma as a prisoner of war and the self-loathing that he harbours as a result of ‘failing’ added so much depth and complexity to his character that enables me to better understand him throughout his many struggles. It becomes very clear early in his journey that Archer is shouldering the immense burden and responsibility for losing the first war against a foe that seeks to change the world as they know it for the worst. The self-imposed guilt he feels largely impacts him as a character as we see this being regularly implemented in the way he regards his own self-worth and the way he desperately tries to keep people at a distance. I found Archer to be very interesting and mysterious as there was clearly a lot more to his character than what he was initially letting on, and there’s no denying that I greatly enjoyed the information that we are granted throughout this instalment. Archer is a revered immortal whose fire wielding abilities have earned him great prestige both on and outwith the battlefield. His capacity to be both a ruthless warrior whom is unafraid to lean into his darkest attributes to ensure survival alongside his ability to showcase warmth, vulnerability and compassion was reflected with ease. I had the best time getting to learn about the many layers to Archer’s character and I cannot wait to see what more is waiting to be uncovered in the continuation of his story.

I had the absolute best time getting to explore the relationship development between Saige and Archer as what begins as a transactional and self-motivated bargain with mutually beneficial gains, slowly develops into a tender connection that leaves you yearning for more. Scheuerer knows how to create magnetic and swoon-worthy chemistry that her readers will fall in love with every single time without fail. The mistrust and apathetic nature to their origins felt like the perfect hook to root for more and it was a lot of fun to see their (sometimes unwanted) emotions begin to drive their development forward. Trust is slow to build with their dialogue being filled with ample wit and banter in an attempt to keep their agreement surface level and to shield themselves against their developing feelings. Fear for the future and the uncertainty of the present plays a huge part throughout Saige and Archer’s relationship but there’s no denying how much I adored getting to see them approach difficult conversations with maturity and understanding. Both characters are blessedly written to react with the mindset of fully developed adults that know how to communicate and respect boundaries. Their relationship is far from linear as both Saige and Archer are undergoing their own personal development that is integral to the connection that they’re working hard to build. There are a strong mix of moments showcasing the searing heat and aching longing alongside the several fierce disagreements that they share. What remains true throughout the development of the story is just how deeply both characters grow to care for one another in both a platonic and romantic sense. There is still so much more of their relationship to uncover and explore, especially after that diabolical ending, and I cannot wait to see what will come next for Saige and Archer in the second instalment in the series.

Kiss of the Black Flame is an incredible introduction to The Bookbinder’s Bargain trilogy and I cannot wait to see what will happen next. There are still so many questions left to be answered, secrets to be revealed and mysteries to be solved. I am feeling morose (respectfully) in realising how long I’ll have to wait to find out what will happen next for our characters and the next adventure that we will follow them on. Helen Scheuerer is an auto-buy author of mine for a reason and this new book yet again proves why this remains the case… so if you need me I’ll be staring into the distance trying to hold onto my sanity as I count down the days until I have the sequel in my hands.

Let me just say up front how much I loved this book! Truly a book that could have gone either way for me and I ended up being so wrapped up in this world and these characters. There were so many unique aspects that really made this one stand out to me in a sea of romantasy books.

For one, I thought the villain was actually super cool! The mirror magic had me SO intrigued from the start. I’m really excited to hopefully get even more of this and more background in the next book.

While I had no negative feelings about Archer, the more of his backstory that’s revealed as the story goes on had me falling for him more and more. He is the epitome of a grumpy MMC, but his life is so tragic and this sweet, guarded man just needed love. I ended the story still loving him in spite of everything.

My feelings for Saige were more complex. On one hand, I loved her, no notes. But if I’m being critical, she was pretty protected by the author throughout and did no wrong. I also wasn’t a huge fan of her reaction at the end BUT…I also get it. So while my feelings were mixed, I mostly loved her and truly appreciated her candor that I rarely see in FMCs. She is SO unapologetically real and honest with Archer the entire book, and it made me cheer her on.

But the ENDING. I knew something was coming, but I didn’t KNOW, you know?! The ending was epic but, of course, left me desperate for the next book!

This book has:
🔥Super cool magic
🔥Book binder FMC
🔥Flashback scenes that build context
🔥Slow burn
🔥Forced proximity
🔥Grumpy x sunshine
🔥YEARNING!

At this point in my life I can say I’ve read almost all of Helen Scheureres books, and as I write this review from my iPad, an unread one is staring at me begrudgingly from my bookshelf. What do all of her series have in common for me? I always love the first installment best.

I was pleasantly surprised to see we were leaving the world of Thezmarr where her last two series took place to head for a new one where we are thrown in 200 years after an immortal warrior sacrificed himself to defeat an evil Silver tongued deceiver. The problem of course being that neither Asher, the immortal Azkari general nor said deceiver are truly dead, rather stuck in a parallel prison dimension where the bad guy has enslaved both the general along with several of his people and numerous other creatures while bidding his time to regather his strength and magic. Enter our FMC who is a bookbinder that gets captured to help him achieve his goals. However, a bargain between her and Archer, sealed with a very hot kiss, triggers a series of events and so we being, etc etc quest start, etc etc forced proximity, etc etc, plot. I never like to do a summary in my reviews and I’m not going to start now.

As usual with Helen’s books, I love the character and the writing, I find the pacing okay albeit perhaps a bit slow at times, and the cliffhanger unfairly brutal but as this is my “I lost track” rodeo, expected.

Saige, the FMC is 35!!!! The author keeps pushing her characters age with each new series and I am so here for it. Some unfortunate circumstances have brought her in the presence of the male main character, but I love their dynamic because despite what she has been through and her chronic illness, it has not brought her down, and she keeps being the sunshine to his stormcloud. What really confuse me about Archer is that because of the dual povs, we get to see into his head therefore we already know that he is absolutely obsessed with her. So why exactly is he trying to keep her at arms length and pretending to despise her and dislike her? It felt very forced enemies to lovers but I do enjoy the grumpy sunshine aspect as expected. It’s a slow burn, but the payoff is worth it. I was also very happy about this male main character being very different than others I’ve read from Helen, a true embodiment of my absolute favorite damaged emo sad boy.

“Hey Helen how broody do you want your new MMC.”
“Yes”

As a whole, I’m extremely happy with this book with the start of this new series and I absolutely look forward to reading the rest and finding out more about this world.

Thank you to NetGalley for the arc, all my opinions are genuine as usual, and I am forever grateful.

As a shock to absolutely no one, I loved this!!

A sassy, thirty-five-year-old bookbinder with chronic pain, a dangerous magical quest, and a tortured, touch-starved immortal general? Helen Scheuerer CLEARLY wrote this one specifically for me.

Saige was such a refreshing FMC. She’s capable, funny, wonderfully stubborn, and already knows who she is. I especially loved seeing a fmc in her thirties whose chronic pain meaningfully affects her life without becoming her entire identity, because that's something I can relate to. She may need to adapt or accept help, but she is never portrayed as weak.

Then there’s Archer... A *terrifying* immortal general who is secretly starved for affection, becomes jealous of a dog, and tells Saige to hold onto the headboard (iykyk). What more could I possibly ask for? Their reluctant-allies dynamic had banter, caretaking, yearning, and so much delicious tension. Watching Archer slowly soften around Saige was easily one of my favorite parts.

I also loved that this gave us an actual fantasy quest. The living magic, dangerous trials, magical bargain, and reveals kept the story moving outside of the romance, and several of the later twists completely reframed what I thought I knew.

The only thing keeping this from being six stars was the emotional timing near the end. I believed Archer and Saige’s feelings, but the spoken declarations of love felt abrupt and slightly out of place within their relationship. The final turn also required Archer to make a choice that didn’t feel entirely consistent with the man we had come to know. I understand that it was intended to create a betrayal and set up the next book, but in the moment, it felt more like a decision the plot needed than one Archer would naturally make.

That said, I am completely invested in Saige, Archer, and whatever devastating mess awaits them next.

Let me tell you, the BANTER in this book is the best thing I have ever read. Saige needles Archer at every turn, and their flirting is unmatched. It shows up all the time and takes every situation to another level. I love Saige's self confidence, forwardness, and I resonate so much with the "I'll just do it on my own" attitude. Her inability to ask for help will get her in trouble, but isn't that just so "woman." This story encapsulates what it means to be a woman on so many levels.

On top of the banter, the tenderness and care between the characters had my heart feeling so full. Saige is the queen of gift giving. She is thoughtful and truly sees Archer. Then Archer is just as caring of Saige in his own way. She reassures him that her feelings aren't fleeting and that she sees him while he is hesitant, and insecure, feeling all the trauma from his past. Both have troubled and tortured pasts, that look very different and watching them navigate this and supporting each other was a thing of beauty. My favorite MMC trope is where he falls first, but then also where he knows what she needs and gives it to her - and Archer is it. There were so many moments that touched my soul during this story.

NOT to say this is a sappy love story, because it is NOT. The story is full of secrets, and as they unfold the characters are left feeling destroyed - and so was I. The ending gutted me and left me in desperate need of a warm hug.

The magic system is fantastic and easy to understand. There are mortals and Azkari (immortal magic wielders) - who draw their magic from the Weave. There is the villain who I'm hoping we get more about in the next book, but he is awful - the absolute worst and is trying to take over the world. The only way to stop it is to restore an ancient magical book and use it against him - which Saige is the best bookbinder so the only one capable of repairing it.

i debated between giving this book five and six stars, but i think with that insanely diabolical ending, i’m gonna have to go with six!!!

i wanna start with how hilarious this book was. the banter between everyone had me laughing out loud. the snarky comments with the side characters i loved. “that’s my son” HAHAHA. and daemos flirting with everyone? yes.

i’ve been a fan of helen’s books for over a year now, so when i saw she was releasing a new series, i had to apply for an arc. not only is this now officially my favorite book she’s written, but she completely changed the romantasy game.

this book was such a breath of fresh air. i love that she always ages up her fmcs, but saige is not only older, she’s very emotionally mature, which shows. and i absolutely love it. she knows what she wants and isn’t gonna let anyone try to convince her otherwise.

archer, oh my god. i love me a good tortured mmc, but this man was going THROUGH it. i can’t say too much, but the way he views himself after everything he’s gone through… i wanted to sob for him, my shayla. not only does saige see and support him, but she acknowledges that, at the end of the day, he has to also get there on his own.

you know the song “the archer” by taylor swift? yeah. this book is that in a nutshell, heavy on the lyrics.

not only am i gagged by that ending, but i’m devastated. this is definitely the meanest ending helen has ever written, and i’m actually terrified for how we are going to resolve this conflict in book two.

speaking of book two… i would absolutely sell my soul for an arc whenever it’s done!! with over four hundred highlights, this broke my record for most annotated book, and i’ve read over two hundred btw.

My jaw is on the floor with that ending


I have a feeling this is going to be the next big book in the Romantasy genre.
• Morally grey MMC🗡️
• MFC 35, bookbinder book📚
• God-like race (Askari)/ mortals 🧝
• Grumpy/Sunshine ☀️
• Adventure quest to save a magical book 📖
• Dual POV 🗣️

You guys this MMC, Archer, is chef’s kiss perfection. Dark haired, green eyed God like war general with black flame magic. He loves flowers/plants, his back is tattooed with flowers, he draws in a little sketch book in his free time, wears glasses, and his heart is literal fluff for the people cares about. 🖤
Our MFC, Saige is so relatable. 35 year old bookbinder, who knows what she wants and isn’t afraid to go after it. She deals with chronic pain affecting the left side of her body but doesn’t let that stop her. She has the best found family. The banter between Saige and Archer is gold.

The plot: Saige finds herself in debt with some bad people and gets trade to the Askari and finds herself in an Askari prison. There she meets Archer and is the first mortal to physically see him/touch him in 200 years. A war is brewing between the Askari and an evil force named Malevron. Archer makes a bargain to free Saige from the prison in exchange she has to help him find a magical book and restore it to its original state. This books holds to key to undoing all the Askari’s magic and if it gets into Malevron’s hands he will destroy the world as they know it. The story starts off a little slow, but picks up. It’s is definitely a slowww burn romance, but when the spice hits, IT HITS 🌶️🌶️

This comes out September 22nd, so definitely add it to your TBR!

⭐⭐⭐✨ 3.75/5 stars

"A story that had me questioning its direction, its characters, and even my own judgment… only to leave me completely blindsided by an ending that changed EVERYTHING! 🤯🖤"

A huge thank you to NetGalley and Atria Books for providing me with an ARC in exchange for my honest review!

I genuinely loved the premise, the originality of the worldbuilding, and the magical elements. My biggest issue wasn’t with the story itself, but rather with the narrative choices. Even after finishing it, I still can’t quite figure out what kind of book this was supposed to be or what the author was ultimately trying to convey.
I have such mixed feelings about the storytelling and its characters that I’m still struggling to decide whether this was a brilliantly unconventional romantasy or a story that simply couldn’t find its balance.

🖤 WHAT I LIKED

The worldbuilding and magic system

The Azkari mythology and magical bookbinding were genuinely fascinating!
And of course, the whole concept of magical bookbinding is simply GENIUS!! 😍📚 Magical books, a skilled FMC, and a world built around the very thing that makes every bookworm’s heart beat faster… how could I possibly resist?!
I also loved the originality of the magic system: the fire, the shadows, the mysterious connection between the two main characters, and the bargain binding them together. Even the title feels perfectly chosen, capturing the essence of these intertwined elements!

Saige — A character I somehow love AND hate!
Saige is such a strange character to love… and such an easy character to hate! 😂
When we’re inside her head, I genuinely connect with her. I appreciate what she represents, her struggles, her challenges, and the complexity of her internal world. Her experience with chronic pain adds another layer of depth to her character, one that anyone who has lived with persistent pain can relate to on a deeply personal level.

But then we switch to Archer’s POV, and suddenly… I CAN’T STAND HER!! 😭
She comes across as immature, frustrating, and downright annoying!
And here’s what makes this so fascinating: Archer clearly likes her. A LOT. So it’s not as though his negative perception of her is influencing mine. Quite the opposite!

Somehow, seeing Saige through the eyes of someone who genuinely cares about her makes me like her LESS.
And I can’t decide whether this is an incredibly clever narrative choice or a major problem with the characterization.

Archer — Just how well do we really know him?
Archer is another fascinatingly complex character, and that ending made me realize we’d barely scratched the surface of who he truly is!
Which makes the revelation even more frustrating!! 😂
We’ve spent an entire book inside his head, following his thoughts, understanding his struggles, and watching him wrestle endlessly with the same internal contradiction: “I’m not a bad guy… but I AM a bad guy.”

But then comes that ending… and suddenly, his constant internal battle takes on an entirely different meaning.
What if that duality wasn’t simply about a morally conflicted character struggling between good and evil?
What if there is something much darker behind it?
What if the real villain of this story has been sharing the same body all along?! 😈🔥

🥀 WHAT DIDN’T WORK FOR ME: The pacing and narrative structure
Where do I even begin?! 😤😤😤
I spent the first half of this book struggling with how rushed everything felt. Events, developments, and emotional shifts seemed to happen before I had enough time to properly absorb them.

And the insta-lust?! Seriously, can we talk about this obsession with insta-lust in seemingly EVERY new romantasy of 2026?!
IS SLOW BURN OFFICIALLY DEAD?!

Also, how am I supposed to feel anything for these characters, let alone become invested in their attraction, when I barely know them?!And that’s where the narrative choices really started to confuse me. Why rush into such intense emotions and physical attraction before allowing us to connect with the characters themselves?

I actually put the book aside for an entire month at the 50% mark before deciding to give it another chance!

When I finally picked it back up, I slowly started warming to it. Maybe I’d been approaching this story from the wrong angle all along? Maybe I needed to stop expecting a conventional fantasy romance and start appreciating it as something more psychological and introspective? And for a while, that interpretation actually worked!

I began to appreciate the internal struggles, emotional contradictions, and complexity of the characters’ thoughts. Suddenly, the slower pace felt more purposeful, and I started wondering whether I’d been missing something deeper all along.

But just when I thought I was finally understanding what the author was trying to achieve…

BAM!! 💥

We’re suddenly back to classic romantasy territory!

The big revelations, the emotional reversals, the whole “I don’t want you… wait, I DO want you!” dynamic… all squeezed into such a small portion of the story!

And just like that, I was questioning the narrative direction all over again! 😂

🔥 AND THAT ENDING?!

WHAT. JUST. HAPPENED?! 🤯🤯🤯
Those final 4% completely changed my feelings about this book!

I genuinely did NOT see that coming! And now I’m left with one question: "Was it actually a stroke of genius to draw us so deeply into these characters’ minds, make us empathize with both of them through their individual perspectives, and yet never allow us to truly understand who they are… only to completely mess with our heads at the very end?!"

I STILL DON’T KNOW!! 😂 Despite everything I’ve criticized, despite putting this book aside for a month, despite all the moments when I questioned whether I even wanted to finish it…I NEED TO KNOW WHAT HAPPENS NEXT!! 😱🔥

If book two were already available, I’d probably jump straight into it!
